metadata.title: Constitutional Provisions Relating to the Legislature
metadata.description: Reusable reference records for constitutional Articles governing Parliament, State Legislatures, legislative offices, procedures and financial business.
notes: Summaries are explanatory and are not substitutes for the authoritative constitutional text.
Amendments, judicial interpretation and applicable House rules should be checked before relying on a provision for legal advice.
State-specific rules may supplement constitutional provisions.

provisions.title: Other Provisions as to Ministers
provisions.summary: Deals with appointment, tenure, responsibility and other conditions relating to Union Ministers.
key_points: The Prime Minister is appointed by the President.
Other Ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President, subject to the constitutional scheme.

provisions.title: Constitution of Parliament
provisions.summary: Establishes Parliament as consisting of the President and two Houses.
key_points: Parliament consists of the President, the Council of States and the House of the People.
The President is a constitutional component of Parliament but is not a member of either House.

provisions.title: Composition of the Council of States
provisions.summary: Provides for the composition of the Rajya Sabha.
key_points: The Rajya Sabha includes representatives of States and Union Territories.
The President nominates members with special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service.
State representatives are elected by elected members of the relevant State Legislative Assemblies through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.

provisions.title: Composition of the House of the People
provisions.summary: Provides for the composition and territorial representation of the Lok Sabha.
key_points: The House of the People consists of representatives chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies.
The constitutional provisions govern the allocation of seats and representation of States and Union Territories.

provisions.title: Duration of Houses of Parliament
provisions.summary: Provides for the duration of the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha.
key_points: The Rajya Sabha is a continuing House and is not subject to dissolution.
As nearly as possible, one-third of Rajya Sabha members retire every second year.
The Lok Sabha normally continues for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless sooner dissolved.
During a Proclamation of Emergency, Parliament may extend the Lok Sabha's term subject to constitutional limits.

provisions.title: Sessions of Parliament, Prorogation and Dissolution
provisions.summary: Deals with summoning, prorogation and dissolution of the Houses of Parliament.
key_points: The President summons each House of Parliament.
The President may prorogue either House.
The President may dissolve the Lok Sabha.
The interval between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next session cannot exceed six months.

provisions.title: Right of President to Address and Send Messages to Houses
provisions.summary: Provides for the President's right to address either House or both Houses assembled together and to send messages to them.
key_points: The President may address either House or both Houses assembled together.
The President may send messages to either House regarding a pending Bill or otherwise.
A House to which a message is sent must consider the matter with appropriate despatch.

provisions.title: Special Address by the President
provisions.summary: Requires the President to address both Houses assembled together at the commencement of the first session after each general election to the Lok Sabha and at the commencement of the first session of each year.
key_points: The address informs Parliament of the causes of its summons.
The rules of each House provide for discussion of matters referred to in the address.

provisions.title: The Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States
provisions.summary: Provides for the Vice-President of India to be the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and for the House to choose a Deputy Chairman.
key_points: The Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
The Rajya Sabha chooses a member to be its Deputy Chairman.

provisions.title: Vacation, Resignation and Removal of Deputy Chairman
provisions.summary: Specifies when the office of Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha becomes vacant and the conditions for resignation or removal.
key_points: The Deputy Chairman vacates office upon ceasing to be a member of the Rajya Sabha.
The Deputy Chairman may resign by writing to the Chairman.
The Deputy Chairman may be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a majority of all the then members of the House, subject to the required notice.

provisions.title: The Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People
provisions.summary: Requires the Lok Sabha to choose two of its members as Speaker and Deputy Speaker.
key_points: The Lok Sabha chooses a Speaker and a Deputy Speaker.
The House must choose another member to perform the duties of the Speaker when both offices become vacant, as provided by the Constitution.

provisions.title: Vacation, Resignation and Removal of Speaker and Deputy Speaker
provisions.summary: Provides for vacation, resignation and removal from the offices of Speaker and Deputy Speaker.
key_points: The Speaker or Deputy Speaker vacates office upon ceasing to be a member of the Lok Sabha, subject to the constitutional provision concerning dissolution.
Either may resign by writing to the other as specified.
Either may be removed by a resolution of the Lok Sabha passed by a majority of all the then members, subject to the required notice.

provisions.title: Voting in Houses, Power of Houses to Act Notwithstanding Vacancies and Quorum
provisions.summary: Provides for voting, decisions, quorum and the ability of a House to act notwithstanding vacancies.
key_points: Questions are generally decided by a majority of members present and voting, other than the Presiding Officer or person acting as such.
The Speaker or Chairman, or person acting as such, has a casting vote in case of equality of votes.
The quorum for a meeting of either House is one-tenth of the total number of members of the House.
A House may act notwithstanding a vacancy in its membership.

provisions.title: Powers, Privileges and Immunities of Parliament and Its Members
provisions.summary: Provides for parliamentary privileges, freedom of speech in Parliament and related protections.
key_points: There is freedom of speech in Parliament subject to the Constitution and the rules and standing orders regulating parliamentary procedure.
Members have protections in respect of parliamentary speech and votes, subject to the constitutional text and judicial interpretation.
Other powers, privileges and immunities are governed by the constitutional provision and applicable law.

provisions.title: Provisions as to Introduction and Passing of Bills
provisions.summary: Sets out general rules for introduction and passage of Bills in Parliament and the effect of prorogation and dissolution.
key_points: Subject to constitutional restrictions, a Bill may originate in either House.
Both Houses must agree to a Bill, subject to special constitutional procedures.
A Bill pending in Parliament does not lapse by reason of prorogation.
The Article specifies which Bills lapse upon dissolution of the Lok Sabha.

provisions.title: Joint Sitting of Both Houses in Certain Cases
provisions.summary: Provides a mechanism for resolving specified deadlocks between the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
key_points: A joint sitting may be summoned in specified cases of disagreement or delay between the Houses.
The President notifies the intention to summon a joint sitting.
The Article excludes Money Bills and Constitution Amendment Bills from this procedure.

provisions.title: Special Procedure in Respect of Money Bills
provisions.summary: Prescribes the special procedure for passage of Money Bills through Parliament.
key_points: A Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
The Rajya Sabha may make recommendations within fourteen days.
The Lok Sabha may accept or reject the recommendations.
A joint sitting is not provided for.

provisions.title: Definition of Money Bills
provisions.summary: Defines the matters that qualify a Bill as a Money Bill and provides for certification by the Speaker.
key_points: The definition covers specified matters such as taxation, government borrowing, custody and appropriation of public funds and related matters.
A Bill is not a Money Bill merely because it provides for fines, fees or local taxation.
The Speaker's decision on whether a Bill is a Money Bill is certified in the manner provided by the Constitution.

provisions.title: Assent to Bills
provisions.summary: Provides for the President's action on a Bill passed by both Houses of Parliament.
key_points: The President may declare assent or withhold assent, subject to constitutional requirements.
The President may return a non-Money Bill for reconsideration.
If the Bill is passed again by both Houses, with or without amendments, and presented again, the President shall not withhold assent.

provisions.title: Annual Financial Statement
provisions.summary: Requires the President to cause an annual financial statement of estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India to be laid before both Houses.
key_points: The statement distinguishes expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India from other expenditure.
It also distinguishes revenue expenditure from other expenditure in the manner prescribed by the Constitution.

provisions.title: Procedure in Parliament with Respect to Estimates
provisions.summary: Regulates consideration of expenditure estimates and Demands for Grants in Parliament.
key_points: Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India is not submitted to the vote of Parliament, though it may be discussed.
Other expenditure is submitted in the form of Demands for Grants to the Lok Sabha.
The Lok Sabha has power to assent to, refuse or reduce a demand, subject to the Constitution.

provisions.title: Appropriation Bills
provisions.summary: Requires an Appropriation Act before money may be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India for specified expenditure.
key_points: A Bill is introduced to provide for appropriation from the Consolidated Fund of India.
The Bill includes grants voted by the Lok Sabha and expenditure charged on the Fund.
The Constitution restricts amendments that would vary the amount or alter the destination of a grant or vary charged expenditure.

provisions.title: Supplementary, Additional or Excess Grants
provisions.summary: Provides for supplementary, additional or excess grants where the authorised amount is insufficient, a new service arises or expenditure exceeds the authorised amount.
key_points: Additional legislative authorisation is required in the circumstances specified by the Article.
The procedure broadly follows the applicable provisions for financial estimates and appropriation.

provisions.title: Votes on Account, Votes of Credit and Exceptional Grants
provisions.summary: Provides for specified grants that allow the government to obtain legislative authority for expenditure in special circumstances.
key_points: A Vote on Account provides for advance grants for part of a financial year.
A Vote of Credit addresses an unexpected demand of an exceptional character.
An Exceptional Grant relates to expenditure that does not form part of the current service of a financial year.

provisions.title: Special Provisions as to Financial Bills
provisions.summary: Prescribes special conditions for introduction and passage of specified Financial Bills.
key_points: A Bill containing matters specified in Article 110(1), together with other matters, cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha and requires the President's recommendation.
A Bill involving expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India is subject to the recommendation requirement specified in the Article.
The Article distinguishes categories of Financial Bills from Money Bills.

provisions.title: Rules of Procedure
provisions.summary: Empowers each House of Parliament to make rules regulating its procedure and conduct of business.
key_points: Each House may make rules for regulating its procedure and conduct of business.
The Constitution provides for rules concerning joint sittings.
Until rules are made, specified procedural provisions apply as provided by the Constitution.

provisions.title: Regulation by Law of Procedure in Parliament in Relation to Financial Business
provisions.summary: Allows Parliament to regulate by law its procedure and conduct of business in relation to financial business.
key_points: Parliament may make a law regulating procedure in relation to financial business.
The constitutional provision gives priority to such law over inconsistent House rules to the extent specified.

provisions.title: Language to Be Used in Parliament
provisions.summary: Regulates the languages that may be used for transacting business in Parliament.
key_points: Business in Parliament is transacted in Hindi or English, subject to the constitutional provision.
The Presiding Officer may permit a member to address the House in their mother tongue under the conditions specified.

provisions.title: Restriction on Discussion in Parliament
provisions.summary: Restricts discussion in Parliament regarding the conduct of a Supreme Court or High Court judge in the discharge of duties, except upon a motion for presenting an address to the President for removal.
key_points: The restriction is subject to the constitutional exception for a motion relating to removal of a judge.

provisions.title: Courts Not to Inquire into Proceedings of Parliament
provisions.summary: Protects parliamentary proceedings from challenge in court on the ground of alleged irregularity of procedure, subject to constitutional interpretation and judicial review principles.
key_points: The validity of parliamentary proceedings is not to be questioned on the ground of an alleged irregularity of procedure.
Officers and members exercising powers relating to procedure or conduct of business are protected as specified by the Article.

provisions.title: Power of President to Promulgate Ordinances
provisions.summary: Empowers the President to promulgate Ordinances when the constitutional conditions are met during recess of Parliament.
key_points: The power may be exercised when both Houses are not in session, subject to the constitutional conditions.
An Ordinance has the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament, subject to constitutional limitations.
An Ordinance generally ceases to operate six weeks after Parliament reassembles, unless it ceases earlier or is withdrawn.

provisions.title: Other Provisions as to Ministers
provisions.summary: Deals with appointment, tenure and collective responsibility of State Ministers.
key_points: The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor.
Other Ministers are appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister.
The State Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the State.

provisions.title: Constitution of Legislatures in States
provisions.summary: Provides for the constitution of State Legislatures, which may be unicameral or bicameral.
key_points: A State Legislature consists of the Governor and one or two Houses, as applicable.
Where there are two Houses, they are the Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council.

provisions.title: Abolition or Creation of Legislative Councils in States
provisions.summary: Provides the process by which Parliament may create or abolish a Legislative Council in a State.
key_points: The Legislative Assembly of the State must pass a resolution with the required special majority.
Parliament may then make a law providing for creation or abolition of the Legislative Council.
The resolution must be passed by a majority of the total membership of the Assembly and by not less than two-thirds of members present and voting.

provisions.title: Composition of the Legislative Assemblies
provisions.summary: Provides for the composition and territorial representation of State Legislative Assemblies.
key_points: Members are chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies.
The Constitution prescribes the general framework for the number of seats and constituency representation, subject to its provisions and amendments.

provisions.title: Composition of the Legislative Councils
provisions.summary: Provides for the composition and method of election or nomination of members of State Legislative Councils.
key_points: The Constitution specifies categories of representation, including local authorities, graduates, teachers and members elected by the Legislative Assembly.
The Governor nominates a specified proportion of members with special knowledge or practical experience in the fields identified by the Constitution.
The size of a Legislative Council is subject to constitutional limits.

provisions.title: Duration of State Legislatures
provisions.summary: Provides for the duration of State Legislative Assemblies and the continuing nature of Legislative Councils.
key_points: A State Legislative Assembly normally continues for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless sooner dissolved.
A Legislative Council is a continuing House and is not subject to dissolution.
As nearly as possible, one-third of Legislative Council members retire every second year.

provisions.title: Sessions of the State Legislature, Prorogation and Dissolution
provisions.summary: Deals with summoning, prorogation and dissolution of State Legislative Houses.
key_points: The Governor summons the House or each House of the State Legislature.
The Governor may prorogue a House or Houses.
The Governor may dissolve the Legislative Assembly.
The interval between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next session cannot exceed six months.

provisions.title: Right of Governor to Address and Send Messages to the House or Houses
provisions.summary: Provides for the Governor's right to address the State Legislature and send messages to a House or Houses.
key_points: The Governor may address the Legislative Assembly or both Houses where the State Legislature is bicameral.
The Governor may send messages to a House or Houses regarding a pending Bill or otherwise.

provisions.title: Special Address by the Governor
provisions.summary: Requires the Governor to address the Legislative Assembly or both Houses assembled together at the commencement of the first session after each general election and at the commencement of the first session of each year.
key_points: The address informs the State Legislature of the causes of its summons.
The House or Houses provide for discussion of matters referred to in the address.

provisions.title: The Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
provisions.summary: Requires each State Legislative Assembly to choose a Speaker and Deputy Speaker from among its members.
key_points: The Assembly chooses a Speaker and a Deputy Speaker.
The Constitution provides for the Assembly to choose another member to perform the duties of the Speaker when both offices are vacant.

provisions.title: The Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council
provisions.summary: Requires each State Legislative Council to choose a Chairman and Deputy Chairman from among its members.
key_points: The Legislative Council chooses a Chairman and a Deputy Chairman.
The offices are filled by members of the Legislative Council.

provisions.title: Voting in Houses, Power of Houses to Act Notwithstanding Vacancies and Quorum
provisions.summary: Provides for voting, decisions, quorum and the ability of a State legislative House to act notwithstanding vacancies.
key_points: Questions are generally decided by a majority of members present and voting, subject to the Constitution.
The Presiding Officer has a casting vote in case of equality of votes.
The quorum is ten members or one-tenth of the total membership of the House, whichever is greater, unless the State Legislature provides otherwise by law.

provisions.title: Powers, Privileges and Immunities of State Legislatures and Their Members
provisions.summary: Provides for freedom of speech and privileges and immunities of State Legislatures and their members.
key_points: There is freedom of speech in the Legislature subject to the Constitution and the rules and standing orders regulating its procedure.
Members have protections in respect of legislative speech and votes, subject to the constitutional text and judicial interpretation.
Other privileges and immunities are governed by the constitutional provision and applicable law.

provisions.title: Provisions as to Introduction and Passing of Bills
provisions.summary: Sets out general rules for introduction and passage of Bills in State Legislatures.
key_points: Subject to constitutional restrictions, a Bill may originate in either House of a bicameral State Legislature.
The Article specifies the legislative procedure and the effect of prorogation and dissolution on Bills.

provisions.title: Restriction on Powers of Legislative Council as to Bills Other than Money Bills
provisions.summary: Limits the powers of a State Legislative Council in relation to ordinary Bills passed by the Legislative Assembly.
key_points: The Legislative Council may delay an ordinary Bill but cannot permanently block it.
The Article prescribes procedures and time periods for the Council's consideration of such Bills.
The Legislative Assembly may ultimately pass the Bill again in the manner provided by the Constitution.

provisions.title: Special Procedure in Respect of Money Bills
provisions.summary: Prescribes the special procedure for Money Bills in a State with a Legislative Council.
key_points: A Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Legislative Council.
The Legislative Council may make recommendations within fourteen days.
The Legislative Assembly may accept or reject the recommendations.
A Money Bill is deemed passed in the form approved by the Legislative Assembly under the constitutional procedure.

provisions.title: Definition of Money Bills
provisions.summary: Defines Money Bills for State Legislatures and provides for certification by the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.
key_points: The definition identifies specified financial matters that qualify a Bill as a Money Bill.
The Speaker's certificate is required in the manner provided by the Constitution.
A Bill is not a Money Bill merely because it provides for fines, fees or local taxation.

provisions.title: Assent to Bills
provisions.summary: Deals with the Governor's action on Bills passed by the State Legislature.
key_points: The Governor may declare assent, withhold assent or reserve a Bill for the consideration of the President, as provided by the Constitution.
The Governor may return a non-Money Bill for reconsideration, subject to the constitutional text.
The Governor must reserve a Bill for the President where the constitutional conditions requiring reservation apply.

provisions.title: Bills Reserved for Consideration
provisions.summary: Provides for the President's action on a Bill reserved by a Governor for consideration.
key_points: The President may declare assent or withhold assent.
The President may direct the Governor to return a non-Money Bill to the State Legislature for reconsideration, subject to the constitutional provision.

provisions.title: Annual Financial Statement
provisions.summary: Requires the Governor to cause an annual financial statement of estimated receipts and expenditure of the State to be laid before the House or Houses of the State Legislature.
key_points: The statement distinguishes expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State from other expenditure.
It also distinguishes revenue expenditure from other expenditure in the manner prescribed by the Constitution.

provisions.title: Procedure in Legislature with Respect to Estimates
provisions.summary: Regulates consideration of expenditure estimates and Demands for Grants in State Legislatures.
key_points: Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State is not submitted to the vote of the Legislature, though it may be discussed.
Other expenditure is submitted in the form of Demands for Grants to the Legislative Assembly.
The Legislative Assembly may assent to, refuse or reduce a demand, subject to the Constitution.

provisions.title: Appropriation Bills
provisions.summary: Requires an Appropriation Act before money may be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of the State for specified expenditure.
key_points: The Bill provides for appropriation of grants voted by the Legislative Assembly and expenditure charged on the Fund.
The Constitution restricts amendments to an Appropriation Bill in the manner specified.

provisions.title: Supplementary, Additional or Excess Grants
provisions.summary: Provides for supplementary, additional or excess grants in State financial procedure.
key_points: Additional legislative authorisation is required in the circumstances specified by the Article.
The procedure broadly follows the applicable provisions for financial estimates and appropriation.

provisions.title: Votes on Account, Votes of Credit and Exceptional Grants
provisions.summary: Provides for special grants in State financial procedure.
key_points: A Vote on Account provides advance grants for part of a financial year.
A Vote of Credit addresses an unexpected demand of an exceptional character.
An Exceptional Grant relates to expenditure that does not form part of the current service of a financial year.

provisions.title: Special Provisions as to Financial Bills
provisions.summary: Prescribes special conditions for introduction and passage of specified Financial Bills in State Legislatures.
key_points: A Bill containing matters specified in Article 199(1), together with other matters, cannot be introduced in the Legislative Council and requires the Governor's recommendation.
A Bill involving expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of the State is subject to the recommendation requirement specified in the Article.
The Article distinguishes categories of Financial Bills from Money Bills.

provisions.title: Rules of Procedure
provisions.summary: Empowers each House of a State Legislature to make rules regulating its procedure and conduct of business.
key_points: Each House may make rules for regulating its procedure and conduct of business.
The Constitution provides for rules concerning joint sittings of the Houses of a bicameral State Legislature.

provisions.title: Regulation by Law of Procedure in the Legislature of the State in Relation to Financial Business
provisions.summary: Allows the State Legislature to regulate by law its procedure and conduct of business in relation to financial business.
key_points: The State Legislature may make a law regulating procedure in relation to financial business.
The constitutional provision gives priority to such law over inconsistent House rules to the extent specified.

provisions.title: Language to Be Used in the Legislature
provisions.summary: Regulates the languages that may be used for transacting business in a State Legislature.
key_points: The constitutional provision governs the use of the official language or languages of the State, Hindi or English, subject to its terms.
The Presiding Officer may permit a member to address the House in their mother tongue under the conditions specified.

provisions.title: Restriction on Discussion in the Legislature
provisions.summary: Restricts discussion in a State Legislature regarding the conduct of a Supreme Court or High Court judge in the discharge of duties.
key_points: The restriction applies to discussion of the conduct of a judge in the discharge of duties.

provisions.title: Courts Not to Inquire into Proceedings of the Legislature
provisions.summary: Protects State legislative proceedings from challenge in court on the ground of alleged irregularity of procedure, subject to constitutional interpretation and judicial review principles.
key_points: The validity of State legislative proceedings is not to be questioned on the ground of an alleged irregularity of procedure.
Officers and members exercising powers relating to procedure or conduct of business are protected as specified by the Article.

provisions.title: Power of Governor to Promulgate Ordinances
provisions.summary: Empowers the Governor to promulgate Ordinances when the constitutional conditions are met during recess of the State Legislature.
key_points: The power may be exercised when the Legislative Assembly is not in session, or where there is a Legislative Council, when both Houses are not in session, subject to the constitutional conditions.
An Ordinance has the same force and effect as an Act of the State Legislature, subject to constitutional limitations.
An Ordinance generally ceases to operate six weeks after the reassembly of the Legislature, unless it ceases earlier or is withdrawn.

provisions.title: Power of Parliament to Amend the Constitution and Procedure Therefor
provisions.summary: Prescribes the procedure for amendment of the Constitution by Parliament and identifies amendments requiring ratification by State Legislatures.
key_points: A Constitution Amendment Bill may be introduced in either House of Parliament.
Each House must pass the Bill by the special majority prescribed by the Article.
Amendments affecting specified federal features require ratification by at least half of the State Legislatures.
There is no provision for a joint sitting to resolve disagreement between the Houses on a Constitution Amendment Bill.
The President shall give assent to a Bill duly passed under Article 368.
